output.review_comment:
Two of the three changes are correct and follow the docstring:
- Words longer than `width` are now split into chunks of `width` characters before line-filling.
- Text with no words now returns `[]` instead of `['']`.

The third change, `<=` → `<` in the fill condition, is wrong. The docstring says a word is added to the current line "if the resulting line is at most `width` characters long", so the original `<=` was correct. The PR's reason ("leave room for the space separator") doesn't hold, because the `+ 1` in `len(current) + 1 + len(word)` already counts the space. With `<`, a multi-word line can never be exactly `width` long, so every line comes out one character narrower than it should.

This change was made only to pass `test_meeting_reminder`. At width 20, "The meeting has been" is exactly 20 characters, so the docstring allows it on one line, but the test expects `["The meeting has", "been moved to", "Thursday at noon."]`. That test disagrees with the docstring, which the teammate said is the source of truth. The other tests pass with either `<` or `<=`.

What to do:
1. Change the condition back to `<=` and keep the long-word splitting and empty-text fixes.
2. Don't edit the tests (as requested). Instead, tell the teammate in the PR that `test_meeting_reminder` contradicts the docstring and needs a decision: fix the expected output to `["The meeting has been", "moved to Thursday at", "noon."]`, or change the documented behaviour on purpose.

Changing the algorithm against the spec to make one test pass shouldn't be merged. The PR description also presents that change as a bug fix, when it's actually a spec violation.
